subject: SLO deviation request: async batch job completion windows, retry behavior, and idempotency
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-analytics.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nightly scoring batch misses completion window — asking for SLA exception + guidance

Hi Grace / Marissa,

We ran into repeated failures with our nightly scoring pipeline over the last two weeks. Jobs that used to finish in <1h are now frequently running 3-6h or timing out entirely; we see intermittent restarts and duplicate writes downstream. This pipeline runs large async inference jobs (up to 2M requests per run) and is business-critical for next-day dashboards.

Can Redwood provide: 1) temporary SLO deviation (formal exception) for job completion windows while we migrate to a sharded runner; 2) recommended retry/backoff and idempotency guidance to avoid duplicates; and 3) any logs or artifacts we should share to speed triage?

I attached a short sample of job logs and a spreadsheet showing the runs. We're on a committed Dedicated pool (contract DL-83421) and need something official — even a one-page carveout we can share with our ops team.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Data Platform, Acme Analytics

Team — forwarding Acme's ask. Samantha wants a formal SLO deviation for their large async runs and guidance on retries/idempotency. Key asks:
- Temporary exception for job completion SLO while they re-architect (they call it a carveout).
- Recommended retry/backoff and guarantee around duplicate suppression (idempotency).
- Any logs/artifacts Redwood needs to sign off.

Questions for engineering: what safe language can we offer for a time-boxed deviation (length, metrics)? What operational controls can we put in the exception (max job size, throughput caps, required idempotency token usage)? Also: do we have precedent for this on Dedicated contracts?

I propose we draft a two-part response: 1) a short SLO deviation letter that specifies the exception terms, success criteria, rollback triggers; 2) a technical checklist for Acme (idempotency keys, recommended retry policy, back-pressure knobs). Can one of you draft technical bullets? I can prepare the legal/ops language.

Grace

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Nightly scoring batch misses completion window — asking for SLA exception + guidance

Grace / Marissa / Dev — technical notes below (TL;DR at top).

TL;DR: Recommend proposing a time-limited SLO deviation (90 days) with explicit operational constraints + idempotency requirement. Offer: 95% job completion within 4 hours and 99% within 24 hours for these large runs while Acme migrates. Require idempotency tokens for all job-level retries and a max retry budget per job (3 attempts) with exponential backoff (base 30s -> cap 10min).

Details:
- Root cause patterns in logs: large KV-cache churn + spike-induced batching latency. Long-tail arises when many parallel shards compete for large KV states. We see correlated token-generation spikes that lead to queueing.
- Suggested exception terms:
  * Scope: nightly full-table scoring jobs >500k requests per run for Acme account DL-83421.
  * Duration: 90 calendar days from sign-off, optional 30-day extension if migration proves longer.
  * Performance target while exception active: 95% complete <= 4 hours; 99% complete <= 24 hours; exclusion for force-majeure (cloud region outage).
  * Observable signals for rollback: >10% runs fail to meet 99%/24h for 3 consecutive days OR duplicate-write rate >0.5% after retries.
- Retry/idempotency guidance:
  * Require client-supplied idempotency token at job submission. Server will persist token->job result mapping for 30 days.
  * Retries: client may retry on transient 5xx or throttling after exponential backoff. Recommend 3 retries max.
  * Server-side dedup: if an identical idempotency token is received, treat as duplicate submission and return the original job ID / status; do not re-enqueue processing. For partial completions, follow up with explicit re-run semantics (see below).
- Idempotency edge cases:
  * If previous job returned partial success (some shards completed), we will mark job as partial and expose a shard-level requeue API. To avoid duplicate downstream writes, require downstream dedupe or transactional write support.
- Operational requests for Acme (things we need from them):
  * Sample job manifests and expected shard sizes (please provide CSV or JSON).
  * Confirmation they will include idempotency token on every submit and on any retries.
  * Agreement to route post-deployment errors to our incident channel and allow limited rate-limiting if we detect runaway jobs.

I'll draft technical checklist text you can paste into the SLO letter. Also recommend we offer a weekly health call during the 90-day period and include a 72-hour hotfix window for critical regressions.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-analytics.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed SLO deviation and operational checklist for Acme nightly scoring runs

Hi Samantha — thank you for the logs and the run spreadsheet. We've reviewed and built a proposed temporary exception and a short technical checklist for your ops team.

Summary (proposal):
- Scope: nightly full-table scoring jobs >500k requests (account DL-83421).
- Duration: 90 days, effective on sign-off (option to extend 30 days by mutual agreement).
- Performance targets during deviation: 95% of jobs complete within 4 hours; 99% complete within 24 hours.
- Retry policy: clients limited to 3 retries on transient failures with exponential backoff (30s, 90s, 270s; cap 10 minutes).
- Idempotency: mandatory job-level idempotency token on every submission; Redwood will store token->job mapping for 30 days and return existing job status for duplicate tokens.
- Rollback triggers: 3 consecutive days where >10% of runs miss the 99%/24h target OR duplicate-write rate >0.5% after applied retries.

Attachments: I attached the filled SLO-Deviation-Form.pdf and the sample logs you supplied (batch-job-logs-20270408-20270409.zip). I've also created a short technical checklist below that you can share with your engineers.

Technical checklist (copyable):
- Include job-level idempotency_token (string, stable per logical job) on submit; keep token unique per logical run.
- Limit client-side retries to 3 attempts on 5xx / 429, with exponential backoff (30s base).
- Use shard-aware submits to keep per-shard work <250k requests where possible.
- Route all job error webhooks to our dedicated incident email incident+acme@redwood.com during the exception period.
- Provide an initial sample of 3 recent job manifests (JSON) and estimated shard sizes.

Operational support we will provide: weekly health syncs, prioritized triage during the 90-day window, and a temporary higher request cap on your Dedicated pool for nightly windows.

Please review and confirm if the scope/duration/targets look acceptable. Once you confirm, I'll route the SLO deviation to our contracts team and produce a one-page signed exception. If you want changes to thresholds, flag them and we'll iterate.

Best,
Grace
Grace O'Connor

Redwood Inference

Two quick asks: can Redwood confirm how the server will surface a "partial job" status in the API (so our downstream writes can be gated)? Also, please add incident+acme@redwood.com to our contacts for the weekly health call invite.

I'll attach the manifests once the engineers sign off.

Thanks again — Samantha
